recipes.name: Feta Cheese and Bacon Stuffed Breasts

steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
In a small bowl combine the oil, lemon juice, garlic, oregano, salt and pepper. Mix together. Place chicken in a 9x13 inch baking dish and pour oil mixture over chicken.
Stuff each chicken breast with 1 slice feta cheese and 1 slice bacon. Secure open sides with toothpicks.
Bake uncovered at 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) for 30 to 35 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Feta Cheese and Bacon Stuffed Breasts
raw_recipe.description: Chicken breasts filled with feta cheese and bacon are baked in an herbed lemon oil.

review.reviewBody: AMAZING!!! I cooked this dish tonight to try it out first before serving it at my New Year's Eve dinner party for 8. My fiancee and I both INHALED it. He gave it a 9 out of 10. :-) The only slight changes I made to the recipe was to use crumbled goat cheese instead of feta. I just prefer goat cheese; it's smoother and less salty. It worked very well with the bacon, which was already very salty (I didn't use the additional salt & pepper in the recipe either.) I also used 2 strips of bacon per chicken breast - one inside the breast and one to wrap around it for a nice extra flavor and pretty presentation. I marinated the flattened chicken in the sauce first for about an hour and then assembled each breast in the pan, using a toothpick to hold it all together. 25 minutes was perfect. After plating the breasts, I sprinkled some more of the goat cheese crumbles for presentation. The chicken came out sooo juicy and tender. I give it a 10 out of 10!

This was really good. Few changes based on reviews: Used 1/3 cup olive oil (approx. 5 TBSPS), 1/2 TBSP oregano, 1/2 TBSP Pampered Chef Greek Rub (probably would be good with all oregano), 2 shakes of pepper, 2 shakes of salt, and the juice of a whole lemon (almost 1/4 cup, or 4 TBSPS). I pounded 3 chicken breasts thin, crumbled 4 strips of bacon with about 3/4 cup crumbled feta cheese and one roma tomato, diced. Added the olive oil/lemon combo to the Ziploc bag that I flattened chicken in and let it sit in fridge while I prepared the rest of dinner, feta mixture. Heated a grill pan lightly brushed with oil while I filled the chicken breasts and rolled up. Placed seam side down in a hot grill pan to 'sear' the seams shut. Browned both sides slightly and then placed in baking dish. Baked for about 30 minutes at 350. Served with couscous and broccoli. It was very good. Will definitely make again.

I butterflied the chicken, used goat cheese instead of feta, also used 2tbsp. of lemon instead of 2 tsp. Placed it on top of some Mediterranean quinoa. Amazing and simple! My husband said it was the best stuffed chicken he had ever had. A keeper!

Really enjoyed this but made a few changes. I added herbs de provence to crumbled feta and the crumbled bacon. Then I butterflied the chicken and covered it with the cheese/ bacon mix. I marinated the chicken in the lemon juice mix and dumped it in the bottom of the pan when baking the chicken. Came out great!

I really like this recipe due to the simplicity. The base recipe allows for a lot of experimentation. I've used bacon, prosciutto, spinach and just feta. I like to use crumbled feta most of the time. Now as for "stuffing" the chiken breast, I like to make a deep pocket with a very sharp knife (fillet knife maybe) with a smaller opening to avoid the toothpicks. The filling tends to keep the breast meat tender. I generally season the breasts and pocket with salt,fresh ground black pepper and garlic powder, but I think you can try a lot of different seasoning combinations. I try to be careful with the salt so as not to over season. Without some additional seasoning I found my first attempt to be a little flat. So I leave the salt and pepper out of the olive oil mixture. Anyway that's my take on this recipe. Obviously, a lot of this is per taste per cook/chef. A great recipe to play with over time.

This was VERY good! I marinated chicken for about an hour, used (moist) bacon bits & mixed with crumbled feta before stuffing chicken. Followed recipe EXACTLY and it worked beautifully. When using smaller chicken breasts definately only 25 minutes @ 350. I cooked covered for 20 minutes, then put broiler on for last 5 for some color on top.

Great recipe and VERY simple. I took advice of others and let chicken sit in the oil/lemon juice/ garlic/oregano mixture in a ziploc for a little over an hour in the fridge. I then removed it and stuffed it with crumbled Feta mixed together with pieces of crumbled bacon. Any leftover feta/bacon I placed over the top of each breast during the last 7 minutes of baking. Great recipe, will make again and again.

I pounded the chicken to 1/2 inch and marinated it for several hours. Then I added the feta and bacon, folded the chicken and baked for 30 minutes. I wanted it alittle brown on the top, so I put the chicken under the broiler after basting it with the juices. Delicious!!!

first time we enjoyed bit honestly was not visually appealing. second time I marinated the chicken in the oil lemon juice mixture, pan fried the chicken and then topped with Feta and bacon and covered and let summer in the juices. Hubby said it was a 5 star dinner!!!)

This was a well liked dish in my house (and my kids are picky!) *I only had limes, so I used that rather than lemon.* I will say it is very rich in flavor so less is more. Next time I will use less feta as I used the crumbles and I used too much. I will also add no salt to the dish until it is done as the bacon and feta had a lot of salt in it! (And I love Salt!) The appearance is lacking for a more formal looking dish, I would say. And you should serve it with another food that would help cut the richness of this dish, IMO. I may tweak this recipe and use moz cheese for the kids next time. All in all, a good dish!

I made it and loved it.Then the second time with a couple of variations I mixed some mascarpone cheese with some thawed and drained spinach and spread that on each breast , then I put the slice of feta cheese and bacon slice.
I made stuffed chicken breast rolls with mushrooms, spinach and feta. Italian bread crumbs also. (Could've done without)
overall it looked good but there is not enough bacon and feta

Delicious! I can't stand the smell of roasting/baking poultry. This, however, is the exception. I kept the amounts for the marinade the same and made only 1 breast. It's incredibly rich, so half was plenty for one meal. Thank you for this fantastic recipe!

I loved it. I served it at a family gathering and there was nothing left. My family kept asking me if there was anymore. Next family gathering, I'm making alot more. I switched the feta cheese for mozzarella cheese, my kid's want the recipe. Sincerely, LisaMarie Eubanks

We loved this recipe. My husband gave it a five star rating. Lacking several ingredients called for in the original recipe, I was forced to either go shopping or make a couple of substitutions:. I took a risk and made the following substitutions: Instead of 1 Tbsp Oregano I used 2 Tbsp of Mixed Italian Blend Instead of Slices of Feta Cheese I used crumbled Feta Cheese Since this was amazingly good even with the substitutions, I feel this is a solid easy quick to prepare chicken breast recipe that stands up even with some minor tweaks.
Pretty good! Definately a home made recipe must have!
I made this tonight, it was amazing. I used more feta, and bacon. I also seasoned the breast inside, and out before stuffing it.
I followed the recipe but got crumbled fetta instead of blocks (much cheaper) and in the toping for the chicken I added basil and Rosemary and it gave it a nice flavor!
